newsitem.title: USA: Chicago stadium plan waiting for Bears, state okay.
newsitem.headline: Chicago stadium plan waiting for Bears, state okay.

text.p: - Chicago Mayor Richard Daley's call Friday for a $395 million, mostly bond-financed rebuilding of the city's professional football stadium was greeted with wait-and-see responses from Illinois Governor Jim Edgar and Chicago Bears football team president Mike McCaskey.
"It's the first we have seen of the plan and we want to study it further," said McCaskey in a statement. "No commitments have been made."
He added that a meeting between him, Daley and Edgar earlier on Friday was "a good first step."

Edgar, meanwhile, said Daley's plan reflected his goal for a multi-purpose stadium in Chicago. In February, the governor proposed a $450 million new domed stadium that could be used by the Bears, as well as for conventions and assemblies. Edgar's plan surfaced after McCaskey rejected a $156 million face-lift of Soldier Field, the team's current home, proposed by Daley last October.

Under Daley's new plan for Soldier field, a translucent retractable roof would be added, allowing the facility to be used during inclement weather. The plan would also add seating capacity, concession areas and a Bears museum. Knorr said the new plan could also double the annual amount of net revenues for the Bears.
Edgar said he, Daley and McCaskey have agreed to establish evaluation teams to make recommendations on the proposal.
Under Daley's plan, the Bears would have to raise $175 million for the project through the sale of personal seat licenses and their own taxable financing.
The team had already agreed to raise those funds for the governor's domed stadium plan.

Another $160 million would be raised through the sale of tax-exempt revenue bonds by the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority. The city-state run authority would use revenues from existing Chicago area lodging, restaurant, and rental car taxes to pay off the bonds, according to Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial officer.
That bonding had also been included in Edgar's stadium plan and would need approval by the Illinois General Assembly.
The remaining $60 million of Daley's financing plan would be raised through the issuance of bonds, possibly by a yet-to-be created bonding authority, according to Knorr.
Those bonds would be paid off with revenues from the stadium and would be taxable, Knorr said.

He added that should tax-exempt financing for stadiums be affected by a bill proposed by U.S. Sen. Daniel Moynihan that would eliminate the use of tax-free bonds for stadiums, there was sufficient bonding capacity under the pier and exposition authority's taxes to accommodate a larger or taxable bond issue.
At a news conference to announce the plan, Daley said Soldier Field would be transformed into "the envy of the National Football League."
